case_study_packaging.headline: Dermatology platform locks in $1.18M in annual savings and 6× ROI through Treya’s strategic sourcing program
case_study_packaging.client_problem_statement: Adult & Pediatric Dermatology (APDerm) had expanded to more than 40 clinics across New England, but purchasing remained highly decentralized. Fragmented vendor relationships, inconsistent pricing, and limited spend visibility were eroding margins just as rising inflation and supply-chain pressures hit. With its private-equity sponsor targeting rapid EBITDA improvement, APDerm needed a swift, enterprise-wide plan to rein in indirect costs without disrupting patient care.
case_study_packaging.client_problem_anonymized: A rapidly growing multi-site dermatology network had expanded to more than 40 clinics across New England, but purchasing remained highly decentralized. Fragmented vendor relationships, inconsistent pricing, and limited spend visibility were eroding margins just as rising inflation and supply-chain pressures hit. With a focus on operational efficiency and margin improvement, the organization needed a swift, enterprise-wide plan to rein in indirect costs without disrupting patient care.
approach_summary: Performed a data-driven spend analysis across 12 indirect categories totaling $6.3 million to identify high-impact opportunities.
Leveraged HPG and Premier GPO contracts and ran a competitive RFP to shift the client to McKesson, delivering 27% savings on medical supplies.
Renegotiated the incumbent Athenahealth revenue-cycle contract, cutting fees from 1.80% to 1.50% of collections and unlocking $260K in annual savings.
Consolidated courier, janitorial, telecom, and IT hardware suppliers through targeted RFPs and BAFO negotiations, reducing vendor count by more than 40% and capturing an additional $360K in savings.
Standardized contracts and instituted quarterly supplier business reviews, giving the practice ongoing price protection and spend visibility across 30+ locations.
case_study_packaging.value_delivered_blurb: Treya delivered $1.18 million in verified annual run-rate savings—triple the $380K minimum guarantee and more than 6× its fixed project fee of $190K. Over 75% of the savings ($908K) were implemented within the engagement period, with the remainder in final signature or reporting stages. Beyond the financial impact, Treya standardized supplier agreements across all clinics, put usage-tracking processes in place, and positioned the client for sustained procurement discipline.
where_we_were_unique: Generated the first realized savings (27% on medical supplies) within 60 days of kickoff.
Deep healthcare-supplier and GPO expertise unlocked Tier-2 pricing that internal teams could not access.
Hands-on, collaborative sourcing preserved clinical workflows by retaining incumbents in 7 of 9 finalized categories.
Exceeded the PE sponsor’s savings target by more than 200% while maintaining full operational continuity.
